sources.shortCitation: The Talking Machine World, October 1927, photograph of Wendling and Monaco

sources.title: Pete Wendling and Jimmy Monaco
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.researchNote: The same photograph circulates on a ragtime and popular-song site, which places Wendling at the right and Monaco at the left and gives its own source as the Music Trade Review by way of the International Arcade Museum. The arrangement of the two men is taken from that reproduction; the citation, however, rests on the contemporary trade paper, where the picture appears with its caption in the issue of October 1927. It is the only likeness of Wendling gathered here, and it stands four years before the American song of his that enters the Kaper record.

media.title: Pete Wendling and Jimmy Monaco, 1927
media.description: Publicity photograph of the songwriters Jimmy Monaco, at the left, and Pete Wendling, at the right, made in connection with the Pathé film Words and Music and printed in the American trade paper The Talking Machine World in October 1927.
media.altText: Two men close together in a halftone photograph, the one on the left in round spectacles, the one on the right smiling with an arm raised behind him.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in an American trade paper in October 1927, before the threshold of 1930 from which copyright still runs in the United States; no photographer or agency is credited beside it.
media.publicCaption: Pete Wendling, at the right, with Jimmy Monaco, in a photograph connected with the Pathé film Words and Music, published in The Talking Machine World in October 1927.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer uncredited; The Talking Machine World 23, no. 10 (October 1927): 137. World Radio History archive.
